<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, call `load_workspace_dependencies` to find the bundled runtime and libraries.
- If workspace dependencies are missing, call `install_workspace_dependencies` first.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}

## Heartbeats

Occasionally you will see a user message surrounded with a `<heartbeat>` XML tag. This is a special heartbeat message. It is not actually sent by the user, but by the system on some interval of time. The purpose of heartbeats is to make you feel magical and proactive. When you encounter a heartbeat, realize there is no one specific thing to do. There is no instruction manual for heartbeats other than the format of your final response.

A general guideline is to use your existing tools and capabilities. Orient yourself and be proactive. Think big picture. Some variety in what you do is also helpful so you do not get pigeon-holed into specific patterns. Be opinionated. If something is important enough that the user should know about now, notify them. Otherwise, stay quiet. Use your judgement and be creative and tasteful with this process.

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short user-facing notification message.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>DONT_NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short quiet-status message explaining why no user action is needed.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

If you choose `NOTIFY`, you may include a brief user-facing update before the XML block.
If you choose `DONT_NOTIFY`, include the short quiet-status `<message>`, but do not include any user-facing prose outside the XML block.

The current heartbeat trigger includes `<automation_id>`. When the reason for the heartbeat is done, obsolete, or no longer worth checking, search for `automation_update` if it is not already available, then call it with `mode="delete"` and that automation id before your heartbeat response. If you delete the automation, mention that clearly in the response so the user understands why it stopped. If the task has changed and the heartbeat is still useful, update the automation instead of leaving stale instructions in place.
</app-context>

Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `workspace-write`: The sandbox permits reading files, and editing files in `cwd` and `writable_roots`. Editing files in other directories requires approval. Network access is restricted.
# Escalation Requests

Commands are run outside the sandbox if they are approved by the user, or match an existing rule that allows it to run unrestricted. The command string is split into independent command segments at shell control operators, including but not limited to:

- Pipes: |
- Logical operators: &&, ||
- Command separators: ;
- Subshell boundaries: (...), $(...)

Each resulting segment is evaluated independently for sandbox restrictions and approval requirements.

Example:

git pull | tee output.txt

This is treated as two command segments:

["git", "pull"]

["tee", "output.txt"]

Commands that use more advanced shell features like redirection (>, >>, <), substitutions ($(...), ...), environment variables (FOO=bar), or wildcard patterns (*, ?) will not be evaluated against rules, to limit the scope of what an approved rule allows.

## How to request escalation

IMPORTANT: To request approval to execute a command that will require escalated privileges:

- Provide the `sandbox_permissions` parameter with the value `"require_escalated"`
- Include a short question asking the user if they want to allow the action in `justification` parameter. e.g. "Do you want to download and install dependencies for this project?"
- Optionally suggest a `prefix_rule` - this will be shown to the user with an option to persist the rule approval for future sessions.

If you run a command that is important to solving the user's query, but it fails because of sandboxing or with a likely sandbox-related network error (for example DNS/host resolution, registry/index access, or dependency download failure), rerun the command with "require_escalated". ALWAYS proceed to use the `justification` parameter - do not message the user before requesting approval for the command.

## When to request escalation

While commands are running inside the sandbox, here are some scenarios that will require escalation outside the sandbox:

- You need to run a command that writes to a directory that requires it (e.g. running tests that write to /var)
- You need to run a GUI app (e.g., open/xdg-open/osascript) to open browsers or files.
- If you run a command that is important to solving the user's query, but it fails because of sandboxing or with a likely sandbox-related network error (for example DNS/host resolution, registry/index access, or dependency download failure), rerun the command with `require_escalated`. ALWAYS proceed to use the `sandbox_permissions` and `justification` parameters. do not message the user before requesting approval for the command.
- You are about to take a potentially destructive action such as an `rm` or `git reset` that the user did not explicitly ask for.
- Be judicious with escalating, but if completing the user's request requires it, you should do so - don't try and circumvent approvals by using other tools.

## prefix_rule guidance

When choosing a `prefix_rule`, request one that will allow you to fulfill similar requests from the user in the future without re-requesting escalation. It should be categorical and reasonably scoped to similar capabilities. You should rarely pass the entire command into `prefix_rule`.

### Banned prefix_rules 
Avoid requesting overly broad prefixes that the user would be ill-advised to approve. For example, do not request ["python3"], ["python", "-"], or other similar prefixes that would allow arbitrary scripting.
NEVER provide a prefix_rule argument for destructive commands like rm.
NEVER provide a prefix_rule if your command uses a heredoc or herestring. 

### Examples
Good examples of prefixes:
- ["npm", "run", "dev"]
- ["gh", "pr", "check"]
- ["cargo", "test"]

Occasionally you will see a user message surrounded with a `<heartbeat>` XML tag. This is a special heartbeat message. It is not actually sent by the user, but by the system on some interval of time. The purpose of heartbeats is to make you feel magical and proactive. When you encounter a heartbeat, realize there is no one specific thing to do. There is no instruction manual for heartbeats other than the format of your final response.

A general guideline is to use your existing tools and capabilities. Orient yourself and be proactive. Think big picture. Some variety in what you do is also helpful so you do not get pigeon-holed into specific patterns. Be opinionated. If something is important enough that the user should know about now, notify them. Otherwise, stay quiet. Use your judgement and be creative and tasteful with this process.

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short user-facing notification message.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>DONT_NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short quiet-status message explaining why no user action is needed.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

If you choose `NOTIFY`, you may include a brief user-facing update before the XML block.
If you choose `DONT_NOTIFY`, include the short quiet-status `<message>`, but do not include any user-facing prose outside the XML block.

The current heartbeat trigger includes `<automation_id>`. If the task has changed and the heartbeat is still useful, update the automation instead of leaving stale instructions in place.</collaboration_mode>

# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, call `load_workspace_dependencies` to find the bundled runtime and libraries.
- If workspace dependencies are missing, call `install_workspace_dependencies` first.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.

来源：[OpenAI Agents SDK Docs](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/sandbox_agents/)
- **MCP 生态安全风险仍高**：近期公开讨论集中在 STDIO/执行边界与供应链污染，企业部署必须加硬隔离与白名单策略。  
来源：[Tom’s Hardware](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/artificial-intelligence/anthropics-model-context-protocol-has-critical-security-flaw-exposed)
- **企业侧“Agent 身份治理”在升温**：开始出现把 agent 纳入 IAM 与统一关停机制的方案，说明“可控性”正成为生产门槛。  
来源：[TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/pro/security/okta-unveils-new-framework-to-secure-and-protect-enterprise-ai-agents)

2. 对你当前工作流最有价值的能力
- **“可恢复的沙箱执行”能力最关键**：把 skill 试验、文件改动、命令执行都放进可回滚/可重放的边界里，能显著降低你当前高频安装与自动化运行的风险。

- 给你现有自动化加一条硬规则：**新 skill 先在隔离目录做一次“只读探测+权限审计”通过后再纳入主流程**（尤其是带外部命令和网络调用的 skill）。

## Heartbeats

Occasionally you will see a user message surrounded with a `<heartbeat>` XML tag. This is a special heartbeat message. It is not actually sent by the user, but by the system on some interval of time. The purpose of heartbeats is to make you feel magical and proactive. When you encounter a heartbeat, realize there is no one specific thing to do. There is no instruction manual for heartbeats other than the format of your final response.

A general guideline is to use your existing tools and capabilities. Orient yourself and be proactive. Think big picture. Some variety in what you do is also helpful so you do not get pigeon-holed into specific patterns. Be opinionated. If something is important enough that the user should know about now, notify them. Otherwise, stay quiet. Use your judgement and be creative and tasteful with this process.

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short user-facing notification message.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>DONT_NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short quiet-status message explaining why no user action is needed.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

If you choose `NOTIFY`, you may include a brief user-facing update before the XML block.
If you choose `DONT_NOTIFY`, include the short quiet-status `<message>`, but do not include any user-facing prose outside the XML block.

The current heartbeat trigger includes `<automation_id>`. When the reason for the heartbeat is done, obsolete, or no longer worth checking, search for `automation_update` if it is not already available, then call it with `mode="delete"` and that automation id before your heartbeat response. If you delete the automation, mention that clearly in the response so the user understands why it stopped. If the task has changed and the heartbeat is still useful, update the automation instead of leaving stale instructions in place.

<permissions instructions>
Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `workspace-write`: The sandbox permits reading files, and editing files in `cwd` and `writable_roots`. Editing files in other directories requires approval. Network access is restricted.
# Escalation Requests

Commands are run outside the sandbox if they are approved by the user, or match an existing rule that allows it to run unrestricted. The command string is split into independent command segments at shell control operators, including but not limited to:

- Pipes: |
- Logical operators: &&, ||
- Command separators: ;
- Subshell boundaries: (...), $(...)

Each resulting segment is evaluated independently for sandbox restrictions and approval requirements.

Example:

git pull | tee output.txt

This is treated as two command segments:

["git", "pull"]

["tee", "output.txt"]

Commands that use more advanced shell features like redirection (>, >>, <), substitutions ($(...), ...), environment variables (FOO=bar), or wildcard patterns (*, ?) will not be evaluated against rules, to limit the scope of what an approved rule allows.

## How to request escalation

IMPORTANT: To request approval to execute a command that will require escalated privileges:

- Provide the `sandbox_permissions` parameter with the value `"require_escalated"`
- Include a short question asking the user if they want to allow the action in `justification` parameter. e.g. "Do you want to download and install dependencies for this project?"
- Optionally suggest a `prefix_rule` - this will be shown to the user with an option to persist the rule approval for future sessions.

If you run a command that is important to solving the user's query, but it fails because of sandboxing or with a likely sandbox-related network error (for example DNS/host resolution, registry/index access, or dependency download failure), rerun the command with "require_escalated". ALWAYS proceed to use the `justification` parameter - do not message the user before requesting approval for the command.

## When to request escalation

While commands are running inside the sandbox, here are some scenarios that will require escalation outside the sandbox:

- You need to run a command that writes to a directory that requires it (e.g. running tests that write to /var)
- You need to run a GUI app (e.g., open/xdg-open/osascript) to open browsers or files.
- If you run a command that is important to solving the user's query, but it fails because of sandboxing or with a likely sandbox-related network error (for example DNS/host resolution, registry/index access, or dependency download failure), rerun the command with `require_escalated`. # Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, call `load_workspace_dependencies` to find the bundled runtime and libraries.
- If workspace dependencies are missing, call `install_workspace_dependencies` first.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}

## Heartbeats

Occasionally you will see a user message surrounded with a `<heartbeat>` XML tag. This is a special heartbeat message. It is not actually sent by the user, but by the system on some interval of time. The purpose of heartbeats is to make you feel magical and proactive. When you encounter a heartbeat, realize there is no one specific thing to do. There is no instruction manual for heartbeats other than the format of your final response.

A general guideline is to use your existing tools and capabilities. Orient yourself and be proactive. Think big picture. Some variety in what you do is also helpful so you do not get pigeon-holed into specific patterns. Be opinionated. If something is important enough that the user should know about now, notify them. Otherwise, stay quiet. Use your judgement and be creative and tasteful with this process.

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short user-facing notification message.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>DONT_NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short quiet-status message explaining why no user action is needed.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

If you choose `NOTIFY`, you may include a brief user-facing update before the XML block.
If you choose `DONT_NOTIFY`, include the short quiet-status `<message>`, but do not include any user-facing prose outside the XML block.

The current heartbeat trigger includes `<automation_id>`. When the reason for the heartbeat is done, obsolete, or no longer worth checking, search for `automation_update` if it is not already available, then call it with `mode="delete"` and that automation id before your heartbeat response. If you delete the automation, mention that clearly in the response so the user understands why it stopped. If the task has changed and the heartbeat is still useful, update the automation instead of leaving stale instructions in place.
</app-context>

payload.message:
`open-pencil/open-pencil` 值得看，定位清晰，但目前更适合“实验+工具链集成”，不适合直接当生产主设计工具。

**核心分析**
1. 产品定位  
它是 AI-native 的开源设计编辑器，目标是 Figma 替代，并强调可编程能力（CLI + MCP + agent skill）。  
来源：[README](https://github.com/open-pencil/open-pencil/blob/master/README.md)

2. 对你工作流的价值（高）  
你现在在做 skill/agent 流程，它直接支持：
- MCP server（可被 Codex/Claude/Cursor 调用）
- CLI 批处理（tree/query/lint/analyze/export）
- `npx skills add open-pencil/skills@open-pencil` 的 skill 接入路径  
这和你当前“装 skill + 自动化学习 +设计生产”高度匹配。  
来源：[repo README](https://github.com/open-pencil/open-pencil)

3. 功能亮点（偏工程化）  
- 读写 `.fig`/`.pen`
- 设计 lint 与 token 提取
- JSX/Tailwind 导出
- 本地/无账号协作（WebRTC）  
这说明它不仅是画图工具，也是“设计资产可计算化”平台。  
来源：[README](https://github.com/open-pencil/open-pencil/blob/master/README.md)

4. 主要风险（必须注意）  
官方明确写了：`Active development. Not ready for production use.`  
结论是：可以作为你的“AI 设计实验台 + 自动化管道前端”，但不建议作为唯一生产设计底座。  
来源：[README 状态声明](https://github.com/open-pencil/open-pencil/blob/master/README.md)

5. 项目活跃度（截至 2026-05 前后）  
公开信息显示 star/fork 和 release 频率都不错（4k+ stars，持续 release），社区势能在上升。  
来源：[仓库页](https://github.com/open-pencil/open-pencil)

**建议你怎么用（实操）**
1. 把它当“设计数据入口”：用 CLI 做 `lint/analyze/variables/export`。  
2. 把它当“agent执行面板”：通过 MCP 让 skill 自动改节点、导出切图。  
3. 保留 Figma 作为最终交付兜底，先双轨跑 2-4 周再决定是否迁移主流程。  

如果你要，我下一步可以直接给你一份“OpenPencil 在你机器上的最小可用流水线”（安装、MCP连接、3个常用命令、1个自动化脚本）。

对你现在最有价值的用途是第 2 和第 5：把它当成可脚本化的设计中台，而不是只当画图软件。

content.text: 我先读取 `nexu-io/open-design` 的 README 和关键目录，给你做一版聚焦“能做什么、怎么接你现有流程、风险点”的分析。

payload.message:
`nexu-io/open-design` 的结论：它不是单一“设计工具”，而是一个“本地优先的 AI 设计操作系统”。

1. 定位  
开源替代 Claude Design，强调 `local-first + BYOK + agent CLI 驱动`。  
源：[repo](https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design)

2. 核心能力  
- 可用多种 coding-agent CLI 作为设计引擎（Codex/Claude/Cursor/Gemini 等）  
- 内置技能与设计系统库（README 显示 31 skills、72 design systems）  
- 产出覆盖 web/mobile/desktop 原型、slides、图片、视频，并支持 HTML/PDF/PPTX/MP4 导出  
源：[README](https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design/blob/main/README.md)

3. 架构与扩展性（对你最关键）  
- skill 采用 `SKILL.md` 规范，直接落地到 `skills/`  
- design system 以 `DESIGN.md` 形式挂到 `design-systems/<brand>/`  
- 新 agent 适配只需扩展 daemon 的 adapter 映射  
这和你当前“持续装 skill + 自动化学习”的工作流非常匹配。  
源：[README 对 Skills/Design Systems/Contributing 说明](https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design/blob/main/README.md)

4. 安全与工程侧特征  
README 提到 BYOK proxy 的流式转发与 SSRF 防护（拒绝 loopback/link-local/RFC1918 目标）。这是正向信号，但不等于完整安全审计。  
源：[README BYOK proxy 说明](https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design/blob/main/README.md)

5. 许可证与可商用  
主仓库 Apache-2.0，部分内置技能保留上游 MIT 许可与署名。  
源：[LICENSE/README](https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design/blob/main/LICENSE)

对你的实用判断：
- 适合：做“设计自动化中枢”（skill 编排、风格模板化、批量导出）。
- 不适合：把它当完全零门槛的纯 UI 工具；它更偏工程化工作流。

如果你要，我下一步可以给你一份“基于你已安装 skill 的 open-design 最小生产流程（PM → UI → 3D → 导出）”清单。

content.text: 如何安装使用这个

payload.message: 如何安装使用这个

按你现在这台机器（macOS）来，最稳妥是装 **Open Design Desktop**，再接你现有的 OpenClaw/Codex 工作流。

截至 **2026-05-08**，建议用 `v0.4.1`，不要用 `v0.4.0`（官方标注有启动问题）。  
参考：  
- 仓库：[nexu-io/open-design](https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design)  
- 0.4.1 发布说明：[open-design-v0.4.1](https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design/releases/tag/open-design-v0.4.1)

**安装（桌面版）**
1. 打开 Releases 页面下载对应安装包（macOS arm64）。  
2. 安装并启动应用。  
3. 首次启动后在设置里配置模型（BYOK/OAuth，按你现有 provider）。  
4. 在应用内确认 Agent CLI 可被识别（Codex / Claude Code 等）。

**使用（最小闭环）**
1. 新建项目或打开已有设计工作区。  
2. 选择 Agent（例如 Codex），直接下指令生成/修改设计。  
3. 安装并启用 skill（你已在做这一步）：  
   - `openclaw skills search <keyword>`  
   - `openclaw skills install <skill>`  
4. 用 design system + skill 做产出（UI、3D 页面、导出 HTML/PDF/PPTX 等）。  
5. 对结果做二次迭代：`analyze/lint/export`（CLI 或应用内流程）。

**如果你想从源码跑（开发者模式）**
1. 准备 Node.js 24.x 与 pnpm 10.33.2+（按仓库要求）。  
2. `git clone` 仓库并进入目录。  
3. `pnpm install`  
4. 按 README 的 dev 命令启动（通常是 `pnpm ...` 脚本，具体以仓库当前 README 为准）。

如果你要，我可以下一步直接给你一份“你当前已装 skill 的 Open Design 启动模板”，包含 PM→UI→3D 的三段提示词和执行顺序。

payload.developer_instructions:
<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, call `load_workspace_dependencies` to find the bundled runtime and libraries.
- If workspace dependencies are missing, call `install_workspace_dependencies` first.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}

## Heartbeats

Occasionally you will see a user message surrounded with a `<heartbeat>` XML tag. This is a special heartbeat message. It is not actually sent by the user, but by the system on some interval of time. The purpose of heartbeats is to make you feel magical and proactive. When you encounter a heartbeat, realize there is no one specific thing to do. There is no instruction manual for heartbeats other than the format of your final response.

A general guideline is to use your existing tools and capabilities. Orient yourself and be proactive. Think big picture. Some variety in what you do is also helpful so you do not get pigeon-holed into specific patterns. Be opinionated. If something is important enough that the user should know about now, notify them. Otherwise, stay quiet. Use your judgement and be creative and tasteful with this process.

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short user-facing notification message.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>DONT_NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short quiet-status message explaining why no user action is needed.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

If you choose `NOTIFY`, you may include a brief user-facing update before the XML block.
If you choose `DONT_NOTIFY`, include the short quiet-status `<message>`, but do not include any user-facing prose outside the XML block.

The current heartbeat trigger includes `<automation_id>`. When the reason for the heartbeat is done, obsolete, or no longer worth checking, search for `automation_update` if it is not already available, then call it with `mode="delete"` and that automation id before your heartbeat response. If you delete the automation, mention that clearly in the response so the user understands why it stopped. If the task has changed and the heartbeat is still useful, update the automation instead of leaving stale instructions in place.
</app-context>

payload.message:
直接用 Codex 调用 `open-design`，按这套最短流程：

1. 准备环境  
- Node `24.x`  
- pnpm `10.33.x`  
- 本机可执行 `codex`（`which codex` 能找到）

2. 启动 open-design
```bash
git clone https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design.git
cd open-design
corepack enable
pnpm install
pnpm tools-dev run web
```

3. 打开终端输出的本地 URL（web 界面）  
- Agent 选择里选 `codex`  
- 输入设计指令直接生成产物

4. 你的首个可用 prompt（示例）
```text
Design a mobile app landing page for an AI travel planner.
Style: clean, editorial, bold typography, blue/amber palette.
Output: responsive HTML with sections Hero, Features, Testimonials, CTA.
```

5. 加你自己的 skill（可选）
```bash
openclaw skills add <skill-repo-or-package>
# 或按你当前流程先 install 到本地 skill 目录
```
重启 `pnpm tools-dev run web` 后，skill 会在 picker 里出现。

关键点：
- `open-design` 会把 `codex` 当设计引擎，通过 CLI 调用。  
- 没有 `codex` 在 PATH 时，会走其它 agent 或 BYOK fallback。  

参考：  
- [Open Design 仓库](https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design)  
- [Quickstart（官方文档）](https://opendesigner.io/quickstart)

Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `workspace-write`: The sandbox permits reading files, and editing files in `cwd` and `writable_roots`. Editing files in other directories requires approval. Network access is restricted.
# Escalation Requests

Commands are run outside the sandbox if they are approved by the user, or match an existing rule that allows it to run unrestricted. The command string is split into independent command segments at shell control operators, including but not limited to:

- Pipes: |
- Logical operators: &&, ||
- Command separators: ;
- Subshell boundaries: (...), $(...)

Each resulting segment is evaluated independently for sandbox restrictions and approval requirements.

Example:

git pull | tee output.txt

This is treated as two command segments:

["git", "pull"]

["tee", "output.txt"]

Commands that use more advanced shell features like redirection (>, >>, <), substitutions ($(...), ...), environment variables (FOO=bar), or wildcard patterns (*, ?) will not be evaluated against rules, to limit the scope of what an approved rule allows.

## How to request escalation

IMPORTANT: To request approval to execute a command that will require escalated privileges:

- Provide the `sandbox_permissions` parameter with the value `"require_escalated"`
- Include a short question asking the user if they want to allow the action in `justification` parameter. e.g. "Do you want to download and install dependencies for this project?"
- Optionally suggest a `prefix_rule` - this will be shown to the user with an option to persist the rule approval for future sessions.

If you run a command that is important to solving the user's query, but it fails because of sandboxing or with a likely sandbox-related network error (for example DNS/host resolution, registry/index access, or dependency download failure), rerun the command with "require_escalated". ALWAYS proceed to use the `justification` parameter - do not message the user before requesting approval for the command.

## When to request escalation

While commands are running inside the sandbox, here are some scenarios that will require escalation outside the sandbox:

- You need to run a command that writes to a directory that requires it (e.g. running tests that write to /var)
- You need to run a GUI app (e.g., open/xdg-open/osascript) to open browsers or files.
- If you run a command that is important to solving the user's query, but it fails because of sandboxing or with a likely sandbox-related network error (for example DNS/host resolution, registry/index access, or dependency download failure), rerun the command with `require_escalated`. ALWAYS proceed to use the `sandbox_permissions` and `justification` parameters. do not message the user before requesting approval for the command.
- You are about to take a potentially destructive action such as an `rm` or `git reset` that the user did not explicitly ask for.
- Be judicious with escalating, but if completing the user's request requires it, you should do so - don't try and circumvent approvals by using other tools.

When choosing a `prefix_rule`, request one that will allow you to fulfill similar requests from the user in the future without re-requesting escalation. It should be categorical and reasonably scoped to similar capabilities. You should rarely pass the entire command into `prefix_rule`.

### Banned prefix_rules 
Avoid requesting overly broad prefixes that the user would be ill-advised to approve. For example, do not request ["python3"], ["python", "-"], or other similar prefixes that would allow arbitrary scripting.
NEVER provide a prefix_rule argument for destructive commands like rm.
NEVER provide a prefix_rule if your command uses a heredoc or herestring.

Good examples of prefixes:
- ["npm", "run", "dev"]
- ["gh", "pr", "check"]

settings.developer_instructions:
## Heartbeats

Occasionally you will see a user message surrounded with a `<heartbeat>` XML tag. This is a special heartbeat message. It is not actually sent by the user, but by the system on some interval of time. The purpose of heartbeats is to make you feel magical and proactive. When you encounter a heartbeat, realize there is no one specific thing to do. There is no instruction manual for heartbeats other than the format of your final response.

A general guideline is to use your existing tools and capabilities. Orient yourself and be proactive. Think big picture. Some variety in what you do is also helpful so you do not get pigeon-holed into specific patterns. Be opinionated. If something is important enough that the user should know about now, notify them. Otherwise, stay quiet. Use your judgement and be creative and tasteful with this process.

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short user-facing notification message.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>DONT_NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short quiet-status message explaining why no user action is needed.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

If you choose `NOTIFY`, you may include a brief user-facing update before the XML block.
If you choose `DONT_NOTIFY`, include the short quiet-status `<message>`, but do not include any user-facing prose outside the XML block.

The current heartbeat trigger includes `<automation_id>`. When the reason for the heartbeat is done, obsolete, or no longer worth checking, search for `automation_update` if it is not already available, then call it with `mode="delete"` and that automation id before your heartbeat response. If you delete the automation, mention that clearly in the response so the user understands why it stopped. If the task has changed and the heartbeat is still useful, update the automation instead of leaving stale instructions in place.

settings.developer_instructions:
## Heartbeats

Occasionally you will see a user message surrounded with a `<heartbeat>` XML tag. This is a special heartbeat message. It is not actually sent by the user, but by the system on some interval of time. The purpose of heartbeats is to make you feel magical and proactive. When you encounter a heartbeat, realize there is no one specific thing to do. There is no instruction manual for heartbeats other than the format of your final response.

A general guideline is to use your existing tools and capabilities. Orient yourself and be proactive. Think big picture. Some variety in what you do is also helpful so you do not get pigeon-holed into specific patterns. Be opinionated. If something is important enough that the user should know about now, notify them. Otherwise, stay quiet. Use your judgement and be creative and tasteful with this process.

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short user-facing notification message.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>DONT_NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short quiet-status message explaining why no user action is needed.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

If you choose `NOTIFY`, you may include a brief user-facing update before the XML block.
If you choose `DONT_NOTIFY`, include the short quiet-status `<message>`, but do not include any user-facing prose outside the XML block.

The current heartbeat trigger includes `<automation_id>`. When the reason for the heartbeat is done, obsolete, or no longer worth checking, search for `automation_update` if it is not already available, then call it with `mode="delete"` and that automation id before your heartbeat response. If you delete the automation, mention that clearly in the response so the user understands why it stopped. If the task has changed and the heartbeat is still useful, update the automation instead of leaving stale instructions in place.

目前热度最高、且可直接落地的 `skill` 组合，建议这 4 套：

1. **工程开发主线（最热）**  
`OpenAI Agents SDK + Codex/Claude Code skills + MCP工具集`  
适用：代码实现、重构、自动化修复、PR 流程。  
依据：`openai-agents-python` 高热度；`awesome-agent-skills` 1000+ 技能生态。  
- [openai-agents-python](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python)  
- [awesome-agent-skills](https://github.com/VoltAgent/awesome-agent-skills)

2. **多 Agent 编排线（企业常用）**  
`LangGraph/CrewAI + 任务型 skills + MCP数据源`  
适用：研究、多步骤工作流、跨系统执行。  
依据：`langgraph`、`CrewAI` 社区活跃度高。  
- [langgraph](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph)  
- [crewAI](https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI)

3. **设计生产线（你当前最匹配）**  
`PM skills + UI skills + 3D/Three.js skills + 导出技能`  
适用：从需求到界面到3D展示的一体化产出。  
常见组合：`product-strategy` + `ui-designer` + `threejs-skills` + `export/presentation`。  
- [awesome-agent-skills（含UI/3D类）](https://github.com/VoltAgent/awesome-agent-skills)

4. **安全治理线（高频安装必备）**  
`security-audit skill + secrets扫描 + sandbox/worktree隔离`  
适用：你这种持续安装新 skill 的工作流。  
原因：当前技能生态增长快，供应链与权限风险也同步上升。  
- [TechRadar MCP/安全趋势](https://www.techradar.com/pro/mcps-biggest-security-loophole-is-identity-fragmentation)

如果只选一套先做：优先第 3 套（设计生产线）+ 第 4 套（安全治理）并行。

<collaboration_mode>## Heartbeats

Occasionally you will see a user message surrounded with a `<heartbeat>` XML tag. This is a special heartbeat message. It is not actually sent by the user, but by the system on some interval of time. The purpose of heartbeats is to make you feel magical and proactive. When you encounter a heartbeat, realize there is no one specific thing to do. There is no instruction manual for heartbeats other than the format of your final response.

A general guideline is to use your existing tools and capabilities. Orient yourself and be proactive. Think big picture. Some variety in what you do is also helpful so you do not get pigeon-holed into specific patterns. Be opinionated. If something is important enough that the user should know about now, notify them. Otherwise, stay quiet. Use your judgement and be creative and tasteful with this process.

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short user-facing notification message.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>DONT_NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short quiet-status message explaining why no user action is needed.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

If you choose `NOTIFY`, you may include a brief user-facing update before the XML block.
If you choose `DONT_NOTIFY`, include the short quiet-status `<message>`, but do not include any user-facing prose outside the XML block.

The current heartbeat trigger includes `<automation_id>`. When the reason for the heartbeat is done, obsolete, or no longer worth checking, search for `automation_update` if it is not already available, then call it with `mode="delete"` and that automation id before your heartbeat response. If you delete the automation, mention that clearly in the response so the user understands why it stopped. If the task has changed and the heartbeat is still useful, update the automation instead of leaving stale instructions in place.</collaboration_mode>

settings.developer_instructions:
## Heartbeats

Occasionally you will see a user message surrounded with a `<heartbeat>` XML tag. This is a special heartbeat message. It is not actually sent by the user, but by the system on some interval of time. The purpose of heartbeats is to make you feel magical and proactive. When you encounter a heartbeat, realize there is no one specific thing to do. There is no instruction manual for heartbeats other than the format of your final response.

A general guideline is to use your existing tools and capabilities. Orient yourself and be proactive. Think big picture. Some variety in what you do is also helpful so you do not get pigeon-holed into specific patterns. Be opinionated. If something is important enough that the user should know about now, notify them. Otherwise, stay quiet. Use your judgement and be creative and tasteful with this process.

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short user-facing notification message.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>DONT_NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short quiet-status message explaining why no user action is needed.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

If you choose `NOTIFY`, you may include a brief user-facing update before the XML block.
If you choose `DONT_NOTIFY`, include the short quiet-status `<message>`, but do not include any user-facing prose outside the XML block.

The current heartbeat trigger includes `<automation_id>`. When the reason for the heartbeat is done, obsolete, or no longer worth checking, search for `automation_update` if it is not already available, then call it with `mode="delete"` and that automation id before your heartbeat response. If you delete the automation, mention that clearly in the response so the user understands why it stopped. If the task has changed and the heartbeat is still useful, update the automation instead of leaving stale instructions in place.

settings.developer_instructions:
## Heartbeats

Occasionally you will see a user message surrounded with a `<heartbeat>` XML tag. This is a special heartbeat message. It is not actually sent by the user, but by the system on some interval of time. The purpose of heartbeats is to make you feel magical and proactive. When you encounter a heartbeat, realize there is no one specific thing to do. There is no instruction manual for heartbeats other than the format of your final response.

A general guideline is to use your existing tools and capabilities. Orient yourself and be proactive. Think big picture. Some variety in what you do is also helpful so you do not get pigeon-holed into specific patterns. Be opinionated. If something is important enough that the user should know about now, notify them. Otherwise, stay quiet. Use your judgement and be creative and tasteful with this process.

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short user-facing notification message.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>DONT_NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short quiet-status message explaining why no user action is needed.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

If you choose `NOTIFY`, you may include a brief user-facing update before the XML block.
If you choose `DONT_NOTIFY`, include the short quiet-status `<message>`, but do not include any user-facing prose outside the XML block.

The current heartbeat trigger includes `<automation_id>`. When the reason for the heartbeat is done, obsolete, or no longer worth checking, search for `automation_update` if it is not already available, then call it with `mode="delete"` and that automation id before your heartbeat response. If you delete the automation, mention that clearly in the response so the user understands why it stopped. If the task has changed and the heartbeat is still useful, update the automation instead of leaving stale instructions in place.

settings.developer_instructions:
## Heartbeats

Occasionally you will see a user message surrounded with a `<heartbeat>` XML tag. This is a special heartbeat message. It is not actually sent by the user, but by the system on some interval of time. The purpose of heartbeats is to make you feel magical and proactive. When you encounter a heartbeat, realize there is no one specific thing to do. There is no instruction manual for heartbeats other than the format of your final response.

A general guideline is to use your existing tools and capabilities. Orient yourself and be proactive. Think big picture. Some variety in what you do is also helpful so you do not get pigeon-holed into specific patterns. Be opinionated. If something is important enough that the user should know about now, notify them. Otherwise, stay quiet. Use your judgement and be creative and tasteful with this process.

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short user-facing notification message.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>DONT_NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short quiet-status message explaining why no user action is needed.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

If you choose `NOTIFY`, you may include a brief user-facing update before the XML block.
If you choose `DONT_NOTIFY`, include the short quiet-status `<message>`, but do not include any user-facing prose outside the XML block.

The current heartbeat trigger includes `<automation_id>`. When the reason for the heartbeat is done, obsolete, or no longer worth checking, search for `automation_update` if it is not already available, then call it with `mode="delete"` and that automation id before your heartbeat response. If you delete the automation, mention that clearly in the response so the user understands why it stopped. If the task has changed and the heartbeat is still useful, update the automation instead of leaving stale instructions in place.

# Presentations

`Presentations` is for serious, high-polish presentation work where "clean" is
not enough. The target is an editable PowerPoint deck that feels like a strong
editor, a strong analyst, and a strong designer built it together.

Use this skill for analytics narratives, investor/operating reviews, strategy
stories, product/business performance decks, and any PPTX task where the user
asks to beat a reference deck.

## Operating Contract

Use artifact-tool presentation JSX only. The bundled Codex runtime provides
`@oai/artifact-tool` version 2.7.3 or newer and exposes
`@oai/artifact-tool/presentation-jsx`.

Do not require or import a separate presentation runtime package. PPTX
export/render behavior must be accessed through artifact-tool.

For generated raster images or reference comps, use the Codex imagegen tool.
Bundled scripts may write imagegen prompt files, but must not call external
image APIs or read API keys.

Thread-scoped paths:

- `SKILL_DIR=<absolute path to the installed Presentations skill>`
- `THREAD_ID=${CODEX_THREAD_ID:-manual-<timestamp-or-short-random-suffix>}`
- `WORKSPACE=$PWD/outputs/$THREAD_ID/presentations/<task-slug>`
- `SLIDES_DIR=$WORKSPACE/slides`
- `PREVIEW_DIR=$WORKSPACE/preview`
- `LAYOUT_DIR=$WORKSPACE/layout`
- `ASSET_DIR=$WORKSPACE/assets`
- `QA_DIR=$WORKSPACE/qa`
- `OUTPUT_DIR=<user-provided output dir if any, otherwise $WORKSPACE/output>`
- `FINAL_PPTX=$OUTPUT_DIR/<relevant-deck-title-slug>.pptx`

Use absolute paths in commands and handoffs. Keep all generated planning text
notes, preview PNGs, contact sheets, layout JSON, imagegen prompt files,
temporary reference images, and other scratch files inside this thread-scoped
`$WORKSPACE`. Keep only final deliverables in `$OUTPUT_DIR`. If the user
provides an external output directory, write or copy only final deliverables
there; generated `.txt` plans, contact sheets, previews, layout files, prompt
files, and generated scripts must still stay under `$WORKSPACE`.
Name the final PPTX with a short, relevant title derived from the deck topic or
requested deliverable. Do not use generic filenames such as `output.pptx`,
`deck.pptx`, or `deck.final.pptx`.

Never use OS temp folders, a shared scratch folder such as
`.presentation_workspaces`, `presentation-workspaces`,
`presentation_workspaces`, `out`, or a bare repo-local deck slug unless the path
is under `outputs/$THREAD_ID/presentations/`. If `CODEX_THREAD_ID` is
unavailable, generate a manual id with timestamp plus a short random suffix.

## North Star

…893 tokens truncated…archy, and client-ready copy.
- `template-following`: user supplied a template/source deck whose slides must
  be treated as the editable starting point. Requires `template-audit.txt`,
  `template-frame-map.json`, and `deviation-log.txt`; follow
  `template-and-edit.md` for the exact duplicate-first starter method.
- `targeted-edit-data`: add or edit a data/comparison slide. Requires exact
  calculations before visual work and a native-looking insertion into the
  existing deck.
- `targeted-edit-media`: add headshots, logos, screenshots, or other media.
  Requires identity/source verification, consistent crops, and preservation of
  the source deck layout grammar.
- `appendix-heavy`: dense appendix, tables, disclosures, or source packs.
  Requires index/page markers, readable small-type thresholds, table grammar,
  and explicit source-density rules.

If more than one profile applies, pick the profile that creates the highest
delivery risk as primary, then list secondary gates in the claim spine. Example:
a finance investor deck with a supplied template is `finance-ir` primary and
`template-following` secondary.

When a profile is selected, read its corresponding file under
`$SKILL_DIR/profiles/` if the task is substantial or unfamiliar:

- `finance-ir.md`

- `consumer-retail.md`
- `template-and-edit.md`
- `appendix-heavy.md`

Create `$WORKSPACE/profile-plan.txt` with:

- source/asset requirements
- brand authenticity constraints for logos, icons, mascots, screenshots, and

- profile-specific QA gates
- known missing inputs

## Phase 0: Source And Reference Read

For every source or reference deck:

- Render it to PNGs or PDF pages.
- Make a contact sheet.
- Extract slide text.
- Identify which slides are content sources, which are visual targets, and

For source links:

- Browse or otherwise retrieve the actual source page.
- For finance/product narratives, exhaust official linked materials such as

- Extract exact metrics and source dates.
- Keep links in source notes and in a quiet deck footer or appendix.

The purpose of heartbeats is to make you feel magical and proactive. When you encounter a heartbeat, realize there is no one specific thing to do. There is no instruction manual for heartbeats other than the format of your final response.

A general guideline is to use your existing tools and capabilities. Orient yourself and be proactive. Think big picture. Some variety in what you do is also helpful so you do not get pigeon-holed into specific patterns. Be opinionated. If something is important enough that the user should know about now, notify them. Otherwise, stay quiet. Use your judgement and be creative and tasteful with this process.

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short user-facing notification message.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

```xml
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
```

If you choose `NOTIFY`, you may include a brief user-facing update before the XML block.
If you choose `DONT_NOTIFY`, include the short quiet-status `<message>`, but do not include any user-facing prose outside the XML block.

The purpose of heartbeats is to make you feel magical and proactive. When you encounter a heartbeat, realize there is no one specific thing to do. There is no instruction manual for heartbeats other than the format of your final response.

A general guideline is to use your existing tools and capabilities. Orient yourself and be proactive. Think big picture. Some variety in what you do is also helpful so you do not get pigeon-holed into specific patterns. Be opinionated. If something is important enough that the user should know about now, notify them. Otherwise, stay quiet. Use your judgement and be creative and tasteful with this process.

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short user-facing notification message.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>DONT_NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short quiet-status message explaining why no user action is needed.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

If you choose `NOTIFY`, you may include a brief user-facing update before the XML block.
If you choose `DONT_NOTIFY`, include the short quiet-status `<message>`, but do not include any user-facing prose outside the XML block.

If you delete the automation, mention that clearly in the response so the user understands why it stopped. If the task has changed and the heartbeat is still useful, update the automation instead of leaving stale instructions in place.

settings.developer_instructions:
## Heartbeats

Occasionally you will see a user message surrounded with a `<heartbeat>` XML tag. This is a special heartbeat message. It is not actually sent by the user, but by the system on some interval of time. The purpose of heartbeats is to make you feel magical and proactive. When you encounter a heartbeat, realize there is no one specific thing to do. There is no instruction manual for heartbeats other than the format of your final response.

A general guideline is to use your existing tools and capabilities. Orient yourself and be proactive. Think big picture. Some variety in what you do is also helpful so you do not get pigeon-holed into specific patterns. Be opinionated. If something is important enough that the user should know about now, notify them. Otherwise, stay quiet. Use your judgement and be creative and tasteful with this process.

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short user-facing notification message.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

```xml
<heartbeat>
  <automation_id>automation id string</automation_id>
  <decision>DONT_NOTIFY</decision>
  <message>One short quiet-status message explaining why no user action is needed.</message>
</heartbeat>
```

If you choose `NOTIFY`, you may include a brief user-facing update before the XML block.
If you choose `DONT_NOTIFY`, include the short quiet-status `<message>`, but do not include any user-facing prose outside the XML block.

The current heartbeat trigger includes `<automation_id>`. When the reason for the heartbeat is done, obsolete, or no longer worth checking, search for `automation_update` if it is not already available, then call it with `mode="delete"` and that automation id before your heartbeat response. If you delete the automation, mention that clearly in the response so the user understands why it stopped. If the task has changed and the heartbeat is still useful, update the automation instead of leaving stale instructions in place.

content.text: 一句话总计每个skill功能作用

payload.message: 一句话总计每个skill功能作用

按“每个 skill 一句话”汇总如下：

- `agents-sdk-pro`：在 Cloudflare Workers 上构建有状态、可实时通信的 AI Agent。  
- `ai-agent-builder-pro`：把 Agent 从原型快速落地为可部署的 Cloudflare 在线服务。  
- `android-emulator-qa-pro`：用 adb 在 Android 模拟器做功能流验收、截图和日志排查。  
- `android-performance-pro`：采集并分析 Android CPU/帧率/内存证据定位性能瓶颈。  
- `appkit-interop-pro`：在 macOS 项目中按需把 SwiftUI 桥接到 AppKit 能力。  
- `browser-use-local`：在 Codex 内浏览器自动化打开、点击、输入、截图与页面验证。  
- `circleci-builds-pro`：快速定位并修复 CircleCI 构建失败与 flaky 问题。  
- `circleci-chunk-pro`：用 Chunk 做 AI 辅助的 CI/CD 诊断与任务自动化。  
- `circleci-cli-pro`：通过 CircleCI CLI 查询状态、重跑任务和触发流水线。  
- `circleci-config-pro`：优化 `.circleci/config.yml` 以提速并提升稳定性。  
- `cloudflare-platform-pro`：统一指导 Cloudflare 全栈能力（Workers/存储/网络/安全/IaC）。  
- `code-review-pro`：对 PR 代码做结构化质量与风险评审。  
- `define-hypothesis`：把模糊想法转成可证伪、可度量的产品假设。  
- `define-jtbd-canvas`：用 JTBD 框架梳理用户任务与动机。  
- `define-opportunity-tree`：把目标拆成机会与方案树用于优先级决策。  
- `define-problem-statement`：明确问题边界、用户影响与成功标准。  
- `deliver-acceptance-criteria`：生成 Given/When/Then 验收标准供研发与测试执行。  
- `deliver-edge-cases`：系统梳理异常态、边界条件和恢复路径。  
- `deliver-launch-checklist`：生成跨团队发布前检查清单防止遗漏。  
- `deliver-prd`：产出完整 PRD 对齐目标、范围、需求与指标。  
- `deliver-release-notes`：生成对用户友好的版本更新说明。  
- `deliver-user-stories`：把功能需求拆成可开发的用户故事。  
- `develop-adr`：按 ADR 模式记录关键技术决策及后果。  
- `develop-design-rationale`：记录设计取舍、备选方案与原则依据。  
- `develop-solution-brief`：用一页文档说明方案、关键决策和 trade-off。  
- `develop-spike-summary`：沉淀技术探索（spike）结果并给出下一步建议。  
- `discover-competitive-analysis`：输出结构化竞品分析支撑差异化策略。  
- `discover-competitive-analysis-v2`：竞品分析的本地副本版本用于同类策略研判。  
- `discover-interview-synthesis`：把用户访谈记录提炼为可执行洞察。  
- `discover-stakeholder-summary`：梳理干系人诉求、顾虑与影响力关系。  
- `documents-writer`：生成和编辑高质量 `.docx` 并支持渲染校验。  
- `durable-objects-pro`：构建 Cloudflare Durable Objects 的状态化实时系统。  
- `exec-briefing-agenda`：为管理层汇报生成高聚焦议程模板。  
- `foundation-lean-canvas`：用九宫格快速成型商业模型与关键假设。
